$description: Directional telemetry coefficients for an AI coding-agent statusline. Core numeric coefficients are {central, low, high, label, source}; label in {measured, modeled, speculative}. low/high are SCENARIO ENVELOPE bounds (every factor at its bound simultaneously), not confidence intervals. See METHODOLOGY.md v0.3.0 for full derivation and the accounting-boundary declaration.

$core_equations.energy_IT_Wh: tok_in * e_in + tok_cache * e_cache + tok_out * e_out (coefficients per 1K tokens, IT/node boundary)
$core_equations.water_L: energy_IT_kWh * WUE_site(location, t) + energy_facility_kWh * EWIF_grid(location, t)

model_tiers.$description: Per-token energy coefficients in Wh per 1000 tokens. Map a model name to a tier via model_tier_lookup below.
model_tiers.$boundary: IT_node: coefficients approximate IT-equipment (accelerator + host node) energy per token, per the Jegham et al. GPU-count hardware-class methodology. PUE converts to facility energy. Google's measured full_stack_scaling_factor (below) is retained as a cross-check anchor ONLY — it already includes facility overhead, so multiplying it on top of PUE would double-count (METHODOLOGY.md 2.2).

small.description: <=20B-class models (Nano/Micro hardware classes): Haiku-class, GPT-4o-mini-class, Llama-8B-class

e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: How Hungry is AI? (arXiv:2505.09598) Nano/Micro hardware-class benchmarks, scaled; cross-checked against Epoch AI (2025) bottom-up FLOP model

e_cache_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_cache_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: Price-inferred from Anthropic/OpenAI cache-read pricing discount (~5-10x cheaper than fresh input); NOT a direct hardware measurement

e_out_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_out_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: e_out ~= 3x e_in, consistent with prefill/decode asymmetry documented across all primary sources

mid.description: ~20-70B-class / 'Medium' hardware class: Sonnet-class, mid-size reasoning models

e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: How Hungry is AI? Small/Medium hardware classes; consistent with Google's 0.10-0.24 Wh/prompt full-stack range (arXiv:2508.15734) for an assistant-scale workload

frontier.description: Undisclosed-parameter flagships classified 'Large' (8-GPU hardware class) and extended-reasoning models: Opus-class, GPT-5-class

e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_in_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: How Hungry is AI? Large hardware class (8-GPU); consistent with 29 Wh/long-prompt ceiling for most expensive observed configs, and with University of Rhode Island's 18.35 Wh (up to 40 Wh) estimate for GPT-5-class queries

e_out_Wh_per_1k_tok.label: modeled
e_out_Wh_per_1k_tok.source: e_out ~= 3x e_in; note speculative decoding may discount this in practice (direction only, no numeric correction applied -- see METHODOLOGY.md 2.4)

model_tier_lookup.$description: Mapping of model-name substrings (matched at non-alphanumeric boundaries, longest key wins) to tiers. Update as new models ship. Unmatched models default to 'mid' CENTRAL with an envelope spanning small-tier lows to frontier-tier highs (the wider-uncertainty promise, implemented in engine.compute). One deliberate divergence from Jegham et al.: they classify Claude Sonnet-class as Large/8-GPU; this table keeps Sonnet-class at 'mid' per this project's three-tier collapse (METHODOLOGY.md 2.2) — the mid tier's band is wide enough to cover the disagreement.

model_overrides.$description: Provider-disclosed MEASURED per-model anchors (LIVE_SIGNAL_ROADMAP.md item 5). These are calibration/display anchors in the provider's own units and accounting basis -- they are NOT yet substituted into the per-token tier math, because each disclosure's workload shape (median assistant prompt, fixed-length page) differs from an arbitrary session. Each entry states its basis so the docs and site can quote it honestly.

gemini-apps-text-prompt.label: measured
gemini-apps-text-prompt.source: Google, arXiv:2508.15734 (May 2025 median Gemini Apps text prompt, full-stack: accelerator+host+idle+PUE; carbon figure is MARKET-BASED and not comparable to this tool's location-based default)

mistral-large-2-400tok-page.label: measured
mistral-large-2-400tok-page.source: Mistral AI audited LCA (July 2025), Mistral Large 2, one 400-token response; includes amortized training and hardware embodied impacts, so wider scope than this tool's inference-only estimate

generation_carbon_intensity_gCO2e_per_kW.$description: Lifecycle carbon intensity by generation source. Context/display data for the fuel-mix and diesel-backup analysis (docs/03) -- NOT a term in the core equations, which use grid-level CI. Median lifecycle figures from IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III harmonization; low/high are the assessed ranges, with NREL LCA-harmonization cross-checks.

wind_onshore.label: measured
wind_onshore.source: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III lifecycle median (11), range; NREL harmonization consistent (~10-14)

solar_utility_pv.label: modeled
solar_utility_pv.source: IPCC AR5 median 48 for utility PV; recent NREL/US estimates for modern silicon PV run 10-36, so central nudged down and range tightened vs the 2014 assessment

nuclear.label: measured
nuclear.source: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III lifecycle median and range

hydro.label: measured
hydro.source: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III; the extreme high tail is tropical reservoirs with high methane flux -- most temperate hydro sits near the median

gas_combined_cycle.label: measured
gas_combined_cycle.source: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III lifecycle median and range

coal.label: measured
coal.source: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III lifecycle median and range

diesel_backup_generator.label: modeled
diesel_backup_generator.source: IPCC AR5 oil-fired generation lifecycle median (840) as the anchor; standby diesel gensets burn ~0.07-0.08 gal/kWh at load (~0.72-0.82 kgCO2/kWh direct combustion) plus upstream fuel-cycle emissions. Backup units run only during outages, testing, and some demand-response events -- the annualized energy share is small, but every kWh they serve is ~20-80x the carbon of the wind/solar kWh they replace

equivalence_anchors.$description: Everyday-scale conversion anchors for display only (report equivalences and the site). Never inputs to the core equations.

smartphone_full_charge_Wh.label: modeled
smartphone_full_charge_Wh.source: Typical 4,500-5,000 mAh battery at ~3.85 V nominal plus charging losses

ice_car_gCO2e_per_km.label: modeled
ice_car_gCO2e_per_km.source: US EPA average passenger vehicle ~400 g CO2e/mile ~= 250 g/km; range spans efficient sedans to light trucks

PUE_typical_hyperscale.label: modeled
PUE_typical_hyperscale.source: Industry-typical modern hyperscale PUE range; well-disclosed relative to other coefficients in this table

full_stack_scaling_factor.label: measured
full_stack_scaling_factor.source: Google full-stack (accelerator + host + idle-capacity + DC overhead) vs accelerator-only energy, arXiv:2508.15734

carbon_intensity_accounting_note.$description: Location-based (LB) vs market-based (MB) carbon intensity for the SAME electricity can differ by 3-4x. Statusline MUST label which basis is used; default recommendation is location-based for a directional/verifiable tool. The static central (345) is a Google-fleet proxy, NOT the user's region — the hourly/regional range below feeds the carbon envelope so the displayed bounds admit that.

location_based_hourly_range_gCO2e_per_kW.label: modeled
location_based_hourly_range_gCO2e_per_kW.source: Envelope for the static fallback: US regional grid averages span roughly 100-700 g/kWh and solar-heavy grids swing ~0-630 g/kWh marginal across a day (docs/02); 150-600 brackets the plausible average-CI range for major datacenter grids without a live signal. Live Electricity Maps CI replaces this with a +/-25% MODELED forecast/measurement band.

region_presets.$description: WUE_site (on-site Water Usage Effectiveness, L/kWh) by climate-class region proxy. EWIF (off-site, grid-mix dependent) is intentionally NOT hardcoded per region as a precise static value -- it changes hourly and should be sourced live where possible (see LIVE_SIGNAL_ROADMAP.md). A coarse seasonal-average EWIF fallback is provided for offline use only, flagged speculative.

WUE_site_L_per_kWh.label: modeled
WUE_site_L_per_kWh.source: Directional estimate anchored to Microsoft fleet-average (0.27 L/kWh) and Microsoft's own qualitative framing of Phoenix as a high-WUE, high-priority-for-improvement region (23% YoY improvement disclosed FY25)

EWIF_offsite_L_per_kWh_seasonal_fallback.label: speculative
EWIF_offsite_L_per_kWh_seasonal_fallback.source: Coarse offline fallback only; hot-arid grids (e.g. ERCOT-adjacent) often carry significant thermoelectric baseload -- use live EWIF/grid-mix API instead when reachable

WUE_site_L_per_kWh.label: modeled
WUE_site_L_per_kWh.source: Microsoft FY25 fleet-wide global average WUE disclosure (0.27 L/kWh), applied as a proxy default for temperate/mixed-mode-cooling climates -- not a region-specific measurement

WUE_site_L_per_kWh.label: modeled
WUE_site_L_per_kWh.source: Directional estimate anchored to Microsoft disclosure that water is required less than 5% of the time in cooler regions such as Dublin and Amsterdam

EWIF_offsite_L_per_kWh_seasonal_fallback.label: speculative
EWIF_offsite_L_per_kWh_seasonal_fallback.source: Coarse offline fallback only; Nordic/Irish grids often carry substantial wind/hydro share with low EWIF, but this varies by year and hour

WUE_site_L_per_kWh.label: modeled
WUE_site_L_per_kWh.source: Directional estimate anchored to Microsoft disclosure of up to 40% of hours requiring active water-cooling in hotter/humid regions

_unverified_third_party_claim_do_not_use.note: A third-party (non-Microsoft-primary) blog cites Microsoft Arizona at 1.52 L/kWh vs Singapore at 0.02 L/kWh. This pairing could not be corroborated against Microsoft's own published tables and is NOT used as a coefficient input. See METHODOLOGY.md 4.3 for full discussion.

time_of_day_seasonal_modifiers.$description: Directional multiplier guidance ONLY (speculative) for adjusting WUE_site and EWIF_offsite when no live API is available. These are illustrative shape, not measured coefficients -- prefer live signals (WattTime, Electricity Maps, weather API wet-bulb temp) whenever reachable.

overnight_02_06_local.label: speculative
overnight_02_06_local.note: lower wet-bulb temperature overnight in most climates reduces evaporative cooling water draw

midday_12_16_local.label: speculative
midday_12_16_local.note: peak wet-bulb temperature window, highest evaporative cooling water draw

winter.label: speculative
winter.note: many facilities run near-zero water cooling below the economizer threshold (e.g. Microsoft's 29.4C/85F threshold) in winter

summer.label: speculative
summer.note: wet-bulb temperatures most likely to exceed economizer thresholds

solar_peak_10_16_local.label: speculative
solar_peak_10_16_local.note: higher solar/renewable share on many grids during daylight hours tends to lower marginal EWIF, but this is grid-specific and can invert on grids with heavy hydro/nuclear baseload instead

evening_peak_17_21_local.label: speculative
evening_peak_17_21_local.note: evening demand peak often met by dispatchable thermal generation with higher EWIF

routing_signal_notes.$description: Informational only -- NOT used as a numeric coefficient input. See METHODOLOGY.md section 3 for full discussion of why price-based routing is not treated as a proxy for footprint.
routing_signal_notes.coupling_strength_assessment: weak-to-moderate and multiply-attenuated; no public gateway currently routes on a carbon/energy signal

batch_api_discount_pct.label: measured
batch_api_discount_pct.source: OpenAI Batch API / Anthropic Message Batches API discount structure
